headline_text: Boston's service portfolio is mixed: core services are functioning, but several priorities need leadership attention.
supporting_text: 50% of scored services are above target, with 9 services in priority intervention. Strength is most visible in Education And Civic Life, while Streets And Public Works needs the closest managerial follow-up.

kpi_cards.label: Priority Interventions
kpi_cards.detail: Services classified as requiring immediate leadership attention

data_scope.reading_note: CityScore values below 1 indicate performance below target; values above 1 indicate performance above target.

score_guide: Use 1.0 as the decision boundary: scores below 1 are below target and scores above 1 exceed target.
The dashboard focuses on the CityScore Full Metric List and uses multiple recent snapshots to reduce one-day ranking bias.
Priority Intervention metrics combine poor current performance with negative recent movement or weak consistency across periods.

methodology.title: Latest score anchors the diagnosis
methodology.description: Each service starts with its latest available CityScore from the Full Metric List. Scores below 1 are below target and scores above 1 exceed target.

methodology.title: Best performers use more than one snapshot
methodology.description: Best-service ranking blends the latest score, the average across available day/week/month/quarter views, and the recent trend across the Full Metric List snapshots.

methodology.title: Worst performers combine level and momentum
methodology.description: Worst-service ranking blends target gap, negative recent trend, weak consistency across periods, and the existing alert severity logic.

methodology.title: Missing services are tracked separately
methodology.description: Metrics without a current score are excluded from best/worst ranking and shown as data gaps so the Mayor does not confuse missing data with poor performance.

recommendations.evidence: Latest week score is 0.10. That is 0.90 points below the CityScore threshold. Recent snapshots declined by 1.15 points. Only 0% of available period views are above target.
recommendations.recommendation: Review queue age, staffing allocation, and handoff delays to recover on-time service performance.
recommendations.next_step: Ask the department head for a short recovery plan with staffing, backlog, and operational bottlenecks before the next cabinet review.

recommendations.action_title: Run a targeted watchlist review for Streets And Public Works
recommendations.evidence: The current bottom tier includes Sign Installation On-Time %, Shootings, Pothole Repair On-Time %, pointing to concentrated pressure in Streets And Public Works.
recommendations.recommendation: Hold a cross-functional operating review that compares demand, staffing, and service-cycle performance across the weakest metrics in this area.
recommendations.next_step: Use the metric drill-downs to confirm whether the issue is a one-snapshot dip or a repeated multi-period pattern.

recommendations.evidence: Latest week score is 1.77. Cross-period average is 1.77. Recent snapshots are improving. 100% of available period views are above target.
recommendations.recommendation: Document the operating practices behind this service's performance and test whether those habits can transfer to weaker services in the same or adjacent service areas.
recommendations.next_step: Ask the owning department to share the specific staffing, routing, queue-management, or quality-control practice behind the current result.

recommendations.action_title: Close data freshness gaps before the briefing cycle
recommendations.evidence: 5 metrics are missing a current selected score and 0 are stale.
recommendations.recommendation: Separate data delays from true service underperformance so the Mayor is not reacting to missing feeds as if they were operational failures.
recommendations.next_step: Confirm metric cadence expectations and add source-specific escalation for late or incomplete daily loads.
